root_cause: Not a bug: maintainer (tiangolo) PR adding a release-automation Typer CLI (scripts/prepare_release.py) plus GitHub workflows (prepare-release.yml, create-draft-release.yml), ported from fastapi/asyncer#608. The statement is the unfilled PR template with only the title and an AI-disclaimer link to the asyncer PR; nothing in it names the module, functions, CLI commands, env vars or message strings the hidden tests import and assert.
best_solution:
Add scripts/prepare_release.py: a typer.Typer() `app` with three commands. `prepare BUMP(major|minor|patch, envvar PREPARE_RELEASE_BUMP) --version-file --release-notes-file [--date YYYY-MM-DD, default today]` reads `__version__ = "X.Y.Z"` (regex, exactly one match required), bumps it (major->X+1.0.0, minor->X.Y+1.0, patch->X.Y.Z+1), rewrites the version file (RuntimeError 'must be greater' if not newer), and in the release notes (must start with the mkdocs front-matter header '---
hide:
  - navigation
---

# Release Notes

' followed by '## Latest Changes
') inserts '
## <ver> (<date>)
' right after '## Latest Changes', so the pending entries become the new version's section (RuntimeError 'already contain' if that version heading exists); prints 'Prepared release <ver> (<date>)'. `current-version --version-file` echoes the version. `release-notes` echoes the body between '## <ver>[ (date)]' and the next version-shaped '## X.Y.Z' heading (non-version H2s like '## Highlights' stay in the body), stripped + '
', with 'Could not find' / 'is empty' errors. Every option also reads PREPARE_RELEASE_* env vars. Reasoning path from the statement alone: the only real signal is the asyncer#608 link; one must mirror that PR's module layout exactly, which is not derivable offline.
acceptable_alternatives: Any implementation of scripts/prepare_release.py exporting the same names with the same semantics and substrings in error messages; internal regexes and helper structure can differ. Workflow YAML files are irrelevant to the tests.

locating_signals: Only the title 'Automate release preparation' and the link to fastapi/asyncer#608. No file, function, or module name appears. Existing scripts/ directory (e.g. scripts/add_latest_release_date.py) and docs/en/docs/release-notes.md hint at where release tooling lives and the notes format, but the test's import path scripts.prepare_release and every symbol name are hidden spec.
our_outcome_summary: Failed in all four configs (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass=false; 46-327 s, 15-24 calls). Every agent patch only added a .github/workflows/release.yml (v4: sed-bump __version__ + tag + push; v6/v7: run existing scripts/add_latest_release_date.py and commit; v8: sed pyproject version + softprops/action-gh-release). None created a Python module, so the hidden test fails at collection: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scripts.prepare_release'. Agents interpreted 'automate' as CI YAML, which is untestable by pytest.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is an empty PR template (title only), assume hidden tests exercise Python code, not CI YAML: produce an importable, testable module (pure functions + a thin CLI) rather than only workflow files. Mine the repo for sibling conventions (existing scripts/ modules, their test files, CLI framework already used such as typer/click/argparse, existing file formats like release-notes headers) and name things by the obvious verb-noun of the title (e.g. 'prepare release' -> scripts/prepare_release.py with bump_version/update_version_file/update_release_notes). Separate pure string-transform functions taking (content, ...) -> str from file I/O so any unit test can call them.
